newsitem.title: UK: Dollar skids in late Europe but traders sanguine.
newsitem.headline: Dollar skids in late Europe but traders sanguine.

text.p: The dollar skidded downhill in late Europe, correcting abruptly against the mark as mounting fears Italy would miss the first wave of European monetary union propelled the German currency higher against the lira.
Dollar/mark was also harmed by a sharp pullback in sterling, which shed four pfennigs as expectations of a rise in UK interest rates receded.
But traders said fundamentals still favoured the dollar.
"It's been a corrective day, but nothing's changed -- Germany's still in trouble and America's still looking good," said a dealer at a Swiss bank in London.
The dollar was trading near session lows at 1.6878/88 marks by 1612 GMT, down from late Monday's European level of 1.6988/98 and well below a session -- and new 34-month -- high of 1.7050.
Dollar/mark's downward lurch finally unseated dollar/yen, which sagged to 123.80/90 yen after a tranquil session spent mostly ranging above 124. It ended at 124.44/48 yesterday.
Italy's lira languished at 995.20/70 per mark in late trade, a far cry from its previous close here of 987.00/50.
"The lira's fallen out of bed and the mark's benefiting from that..but nothing fundamentally has changed in perceptions of the dollar," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB here.

The lira's slide beneath its central ERM parity rate of 990 per mark was sparked by a mix of comments from Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Monday and reported newspaper remarks by Belgian central bank chief Alfonse Verplaetse, traders said.
Verplaetse denied the report in Belgium's De Financieel Economische Tijd, which quoted him as saying EMU should start without Italy since Rome would flunk budget deficit criteria.

In the wake of Prodi's outspoken allegation yesterday that Germany was less committed than Italy to EMU, the market was eagerly awaiting a speech by German finance secretary Juergen Stark, scheduled for 1645 GMT.
"It is unlikely that in this climate Stark's speech this afternoon will pull any punches over Italian EMU aspirations," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered here.
The peseta fell in the lira's slipstream to 84.74/75 per mark by 1643 GMT from late Monday's level here of 84.57. Dealers said the Bank of Spain had bought pesetas for marks around 84.75.
Sterling was a major casualty, plunging to 2.7048/57 marks from 2.7446/45 late yesterday, far off its session peak of 2.7535. Cable fell to $1.6020/30 from yesterday's $1.6168/74.
The pound's dive came in the wake of an apparent softening of the Bank of England's hawkish inflation stance.
BoE governor Eddie George said on Monday that a spate of UK economic data, along with sterling's strength, had made the need for a rate rise less urgent than was thought in December.

No major U.S. data were released on Tuesday, but the market is awaiting December international trade figures due on Wednesday. Analysts said the data could force the dollar to pause if they showed an expected widening in the U.S. deficit.
U.S. January CPI is also due on Wednesday.
On Thursday, the German Ifo survey for January will be a key factor for dollar/mark, analysts said.
"As long as the perception is the U.S. economy is growing at a fairly healthy pace and the German economy remains weak, the dollar's going to continue to gain ground," said DKB's Stamenkovic.

Dollar/yen should find penetration of 125 tough, however, as the market remains wary of possible Bank of Japan intervention, analysts said. The market was spooked earlier this week by a report saying the U.S. and Japan had agreed Japan would intervene unilaterally in the market if the yen fell sharply.
-- Abigail Levene, London Newsroom +44-171-542-8968
